title: A multicenter, single-arm phase II study to assess the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of Isatuximab in adult patients with cytologic or molecular relapsed/refractory CD38 positive T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
official: A multicenter, single-arm phase II study to assess the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of Isatuximab in adult patients with cytologic or molecular relapsed/refractory CD38 positive T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
summary:
Main objective: Cohort 1: To evaluate safety and efficacy of Isatuximab as part of a combination chemotherapy regimen
for R/R T-ALL/T-LBL
Cohort 2: To evaluate the efficacy of Isatuximab as single drug to induce molecular remission (MolCR)
combined in MRD+ ALL - terminated with protocol version 3.0.
conditions: Cytologic or molecular relapsed/refractory CD38 positive T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia

interventions.name: SARCLISA 20mg/mL concentrate for solution for infusion.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients with CD38 positive T-ALL fitting either to the definitions for 1 or 2:
2. Adequate renal function defined as follows: - Serum creatinine ≤ 2 x ULN; - Any serum creatinine level associated with a calculated creatinine clearance >= 40 mL/min
3. Negative pregnancy test in women of childbearing potential (WOCBP)
4. WOCBP must commit to either abstain continuously from heterosexual sexual intercourse or to use 2 methods of reliable birth control simultaneously
5. Men who are sexually active with a WOCBP must agree to use a barrier method of contraception
6. Participation in the registry of the German Multicenter Study Group for Adult ALL (GMALL)
7. 1: Either: In relapse or with primary refractory disease defined as ≥5% blasts in bone marrow cytology or ≥1% minimal residual disease (MRD)
8. 2: Or: Extramedullary relapse or primary refractory disease confirmed by standard imaging with measurable target leasions
9. ECOG status: 0-2
10. Age at least 18 years or older
11. Evidence of a personally signed and dated informed consent indication that the patient has been informed of all pertinent aspects of the study
12. Patient must be willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests and other study procedures
13. Regeneration from last chemotherapy defined as follows: -Platelets >=10.000/µL (platelet transfusion allowed); - Hemoglobin >=7.5 g/dL (red blood cell transfusion allowed)
14. Adequate liver function defined as follows: - Bilirubin ≤ 1.5 ULN (unless Gilbert Meulengracht disease or classified as result of liver infiltration by investigator); - AST and ALT ≤ 2.5 x ULN (unless classified as result of liver infiltration by investigator)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients with CNS-only relapse
2. Treatment with an investigational agent within 4 weeks from start of study treatment (safety follow-up period of respective study)
3. Concurrent active malignancy other than non-melanoma skin cancer, carcinoma in situ of the cervix, or localized prostate cancer that has been treated with radiation or surgery; patients with previous malignancies are eligible if they have been disease free for >= 2 years and do not require any antitumor therapy
4. Evidence of uncontrolled current serious active infection or recent history (within 4 months) of deep tissue infections such as fasciitis or osteomyelitis
5. Known allergies, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to Boron or Mannitol, corticosteroids, mAb (including Isatuximab) or human proteins, or their excipients (refer to respective Summary of Product Characteristics), or known sensitivity to mammalian-derived products
6. Active infection, any other concurrent disease or medical condition that are deemed to interfere with the conduct of the study as judged by the investigator
7. Pregnant or breastfeeding females
8. Vaccination with live attenuated vaccines within 4 weeks of first study agent administration
9. Other severe acute or chronic medical or psychiatric condition or laboratory abnormality that may increase the risk associated with study participation or investigational product administration or may interfere with the interpretation of study results and, in the judgement of the investigator, would make the patient inappropriate for entry into this study
10. Patients who have received prior antileukemic immunotherapy within 2 weeks prior to start of Isatuximab treatment
11. Patients who have received treatment for leukemia with chemotherapy as follows: o Patients who have received treatment for leukemia with chemotherapy within 2 weeks prior to start of Isatuximab treatment (exception: documented disease progression under chemotherapy and pre-phase therapy with 5-7 days of Dexamethasone, 3 days of Cyclophosphamide; intrathecal prophylaxis) o Patients who are candidates for a treatment with Nelarabine (eligibility to be assessed particularly in patients with extramedullary involvement and/or early/mature T-ALL/TLBL, due to limited efficacy)
12. Patients must have recovered from acute non-hematologic toxicity form previous therapies to ≤ grade I unless signs or symptoms are correlated to leukaemia involvement
13. Prior SCT ≤ 3 months from start of study treatment
14. Acute GvHD >= grade II or active chronic GvHD requiring systemic treatment
15. Any systemic GvHD prophylaxis or treatment within 2 weeks from start of study treatment
16. Known HIV positivity, known hepatitis B surface antigen positivity or known history of hepatitis C
17. Unstable or severe uncontrolled medical condition e.g. unstable cardiac function or unstable pulmonary condition
